citations.assessment: The available Zohar explicitly names Shemayah Hasida in narrative dialogue in Balak.
In Shin 6 the work explicitly names Shemayah as nasi and calls him a spark of Moses. These are attributed mystical statements.
Ta’anit has Shemayah and Ahiyah as brothers and names the twelfth in its discussion of the annulled commemoration. Neither passage connects them to the mystic.
Rashi’s commentary explicitly distinguishes Iddo from this Shemayah and calls the two brothers pious.
The commentary quotes Rashi’s exact line and discusses the Iddo identification.

holds.reason: Gilgulei Neshamot explicitly cites Devarim. The readily verified Zohar passages giving the name are in Balak, so the printed Devarim pointer remains unlocalized.
The exact identification is found in Gilgulei Neshamot as an interpretation of the elder in the Tikkunim. A matching independently checked Tikkunim passage remains unresolved.
